newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria compensates victims of Nazi oppression.
newsitem.headline: Austria compensates victims of Nazi oppression.

text.p: Austria has paid around half the 30,000 or so of its citizens eligible to be compensated for their suffering under Nazi rule.
They have received the 70,000 schillings ($5,800) parliament has agreed to pay each victim, parliamentary president Heinz Fischer told reporters.
Around 65,000 Austrian Jews were killed in the Nazi Holocaust and thousands more escaped extermination by fleeing the country.
The Austrian parliament voted only in 1995 to pay victims after years of criticism that post-war governments had ignored their moral duty by failing to agree to compensation.
West Germany set up a compensation fund shortly after the end of World War Two.
The majority of applications for compensation has come from the United States, followed by Israel, Britain and South American countries.
